metadata.title: Density Pass 34 -- 15th Alabama vs 20th Maine: Final Assault (Ticks 268-278)
metadata.description: Oates's 15th Alabama making its multiple charges up Little Round Top against Chamberlain's 20th Maine. The 15th Alabama has marched 25 miles that day without water. Oates later claims he nearly had the summit. Company B sent to capture a water detail -- never returns. The final charge repulsed. Chamberlain's famous downhill bayonet charge at tick 275.

placements.notes: 15th Alabama -- FIRST ASSAULT on Little Round Top. Men haven't had water in 25 miles of marching. Oates later: I could have won.
47th Alabama supporting the 15th on Oates's left
20th Maine -- Chamberlain's refused flank holds the extreme left of the entire Union army
15th Alabama REPULSED on first assault -- falling back to reform. Company B still missing.
SECOND ASSAULT -- Oates charges again immediately. His men are exhausted and thirsty but they go.
20th Maine extending left -- Chamberlain bends his flank back, refusing to be flanked
Second assault repulsed -- Oates orders a THIRD charge. His officers look at him in disbelief.
THIRD ASSAULT -- men loading and firing on the run uphill. Some reach within 10 yards of the Union line.
20th Maine low on ammunition -- Chamberlain passes word: be ready to fix bayonets
Third assault failing -- 15th Alabama men falling on the slope. Oates is ordering yet another charge.
FOURTH ASSAULT -- Oates: We were within a few feet of them when...
CHAMBERLAIN'S CHARGE -- bayonets fixed, wheeling down the hill. Great Heavens, try the steel!
15th Alabama ROUTED by the unexpected charge -- men fleeing downhill in disorder
47th Alabama also breaking -- the whole Confederate left collapsing
20th Maine pursuing down the slope -- capturing scores of prisoners from the broken Alabama regiments
15th Alabama reforming at the base -- 134 casualties from 499. Company B never found. Little Round Top is lost.
